name: How much does a home addition cost per square foot in Los Angeles by neighborhood?

mainEntity.name: How much does a home addition cost per square foot in Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, or North Hollywood?
mainEntity.text: How much does a home addition cost per square foot in Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, or North Hollywood?

acceptedAnswer.text: Home addition pricing in Greater Los Angeles is usually driven by three things: structural complexity, finish level, and jurisdiction-specific requirements. A modest single-room bump-out will typically cost less per square foot than a second-story addition, which often needs more structural reinforcement, temporary roof removal, and more detailed engineering. Cities like Pasadena or Glendale may also have different review processes, which can affect timeline and soft costs. Homeowners should compare bids using the same scope, not just the lowest price. A realistic budget should include design, permits, structural engineering, energy compliance, utility upgrades, and contingency. Luxury finishes, custom windows, high-end HVAC, and complex rooflines can push costs much higher. The best way to evaluate value is to ask contractors for a detailed line-item proposal with allowances clearly stated, especially for finish selections and unknown site conditions. A lower quote that omits these items is often not a true apples-to-apples comparison.
acceptedAnswer.description: Home addition costs in the Los Angeles area usually vary by size, finish level, structural complexity, and city requirements. Simple additions often cost far less per square foot than second-story or luxury additions, and permit, engineering, and utility work can change the total significantly.
